catalog_quote: [Griffiths 2008, sec. 1.5 Intonation/Stress] Zide (1965: 44) remarks: “Any syllable of CVC shape, and any morpheme-final syllable in a non-affixal morpheme is — by definition — stressed.” I have no data on intonation or stress to confirm or contradict this statement. Cf. Bhattacharya 1968: xxi and xxiii on the closely related Remo language. ... [sec. 1.2 Suprasegmental Phenomena (Tone, Register)] These phenomena have not yet been investigated in a detailed and systematic manner. Tone is known not to be phonemic, as is vowel length. ... Not yet formally investigated

sources.quote: p.146: prominence falls 'not on the first syllable, but rather the second one in Sora disyllables. It turns out that this is also true of many other Munda languages (Santali (Horo & Anderson, 2021), GtaʔP, Remo, Gutob).' p.154: 'many Munda languages have prominence on the second syllable, including Santali, Remo, Gtaʔ, Gutob and Gorum.' No Gutob data or measurements given.
